source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 44 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, which ranks fifteenth in Virginia by published megawatts.

The campus carries 420,000 square feet of technical space and seven certifications covering financial controls, payment card data, health information, federal systems, and telecommunications infrastructure. Each certification is a permission to host a category of work, not evidence that any particular tenant is present. The operator publishes no address, no tenant list, no power procurement method, and no delivery schedule.

Virginia is the densest concentration of published data center capacity this data tracks, with 2,563.4 MW across 29 facilities that publish a figure, out of 376 mapped facilities in the state. That gap is the pattern worth holding onto. Most of the physical buildout in the largest AI market in the country is invisible in capacity terms, and the facilities that do publish are the ones large enough to be counted. A 44 MW campus is a meaningful increment to Northern Virginia grid load, but it is one of hundreds of mapped sites whose draw is not stated.

What the data does not say is how that 44 MW is delivered or when. It does not name a utility, a substation, a power purchase agreement, or an energization date. It does not say what density the halls are built to, so the accelerator count behind the figure cannot be derived from anything here. The score of 70 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
